topic: Concurrent duplicate checks and atomic reward recording

source.author: Malcolm Featonby
source.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
source.publication_date: Not confirmed from the inspected page
source.version_scope: Mutable official engineering article, not a fixed service implementation
source.read_scope: All article sections from Introduction through Conclusion and shown command/response text; figures not inspected and commands not executed.
source.key_location: Reducing client complexity: token recording and related mutations must form an ACID operation, avoiding either a record without the change or a change without the record.
source.limits: Does not implement the library's game service, select a database isolation level or supply automatic atomicity across external services.

original_example: Two workers for the same authenticated caller and completion identity both observe no prior record before either applies an unprotected change. This is an unexecuted interleaving illustrating why a separate existence query is not mutual exclusion.
deduplication_decision: Reject a new general idempotency book: existing online-service and economy readers already explain intent identity, retention, result uncertainty and joint state persistence. Retain only the concurrent-check gap as a finite supplement.
verification_scope: Source reading and editorial reasoning only. No service request, database execution, crash injection or original-source command execution.
